root_cause.text: The delay timer reused the same clock event instance (`sched_clkevt`) as the sched_clock, but `sched_clkevt` was only initialized when `use_sched_clock` was set; unconditionally registering the delay timer caused `sp804_read()` to dereference an uninitialized pointer, leading to an Oops.
root_cause.evidence: The commit message explicitly states: "sched_clkevt is not properly initialized. However, sp804_register_delay_timer is invoked unconditionally, and read_current_timer() subsequently calls sp804_read on an uninitialized sched_clkevt, leading to a kernel Oops when accessing sched_clkevt->value." The patch fixes this by allocating a dedicated `delay_clkevt` and passing it to `sp804_register_delay_timer` instead of relying on `sched_clkevt`.

intent_record.intent_summary: Decouple the delay timer from the sched_clock timer by accepting an explicit timer pointer, enabling use of a dedicated hardware counter for delay timing.
intent_record.what: Added a static pointer 'delay_clkevt' and changed sp804_read_delay_timer_read to read directly from it instead of calling sp804_read(); changed sp804_register_delay_timer signature to accept a struct sp804_clkevt pointer and store it; updated the stub accordingly; added a comment.
intent_record.how: The delay timer read function now uses a dedicated timer instance (stored in delay_clkevt) instead of the global sched_clkevt, allowing the delay timer to be backed by a different hardware counter. The registration function requires the caller to specify which timer to use.

intent_record.intent_summary: Remove sp804_register_delay_timer call from sp804_clocksource_and_sched_clock_init to fix potential incorrect or premature registration of the delay timer.
intent_record.what: Removed the call to sp804_register_delay_timer(rate) from the sp804_clocksource_and_sched_clock_init function.
intent_record.how: The delay timer will no longer be registered during the clocksource and sched_clock initialization path, which may prevent double registration or register it at a more appropriate time elsewhere.

intent_record.intent_summary: Register the SP804 delay timer during clocksource and sched clock initialization to ensure proper udelay functionality.
intent_record.what: Added a call to sp804_register_delay_timer(clkevt, rate) after clocksource_mmio_init and before the use_sched_clock conditional block.
intent_record.how: This registers a delay timer for the SP804 timer driver during initialization, making udelay loops functional earlier in the boot process.

bic_trace_step.reason: The commit unconditionally registers a delay timer via sp804_register_delay_timer() at line 138 inside sp804_clocksource_and_sched_clock_init(). The delay timer uses sp804_read(), which dereferences the global pointer sched_clkevt. According to the root cause, sched_clkevt is only initialized when use_sched_clock is set, so this unconditional registration can lead to dereferencing an uninitialized pointer (NULL or invalid) and cause an Oops. No guard or check is present in the shown code to prevent this, so the vulnerable construct is present and the fix is absent.
